cards.explanation: The answer is the first day of the first month. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, “On the first day of the first month you are to set up the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.” A real date, not a vague 'sometime soon.' I think anybody who's ever been told 'we'll get to it eventually' would appreciate that.

The word is holy. The LORD says to Moses, Israel's leader, “Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it; consecrate it along with all its furnishings, and it shall be holy.” The oil goes on, and the whole place and everything in it is set apart. Nothing in there gets skipped.

The answer is True! The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, “Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils; consecrate the altar, and it shall be most holy.” Notice the step up. The tabernacle and its furnishings shall be holy, and this altar shall be most holy.

The answer is water. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, “Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.” Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). Before the garments and the anointing, there's a washing. Think of it like clean hands before you touch the dough.

The answer is so he may serve the LORD as a priest. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to clothe Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), with the holy garments, anoint him and consecrate him “…so that he may serve Me as a priest.” The garments and the oil are for service. I think that makes it a pretty big job.

The answer is throughout their generations. The LORD says, “Their anointing will qualify them for a permanent priesthood throughout their generations.” Permanent, generation after generation. This isn't a one-batch job, friends. It's meant to last.

The answer is second. The text says, “So the tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month of the second year.” That matches the first day of the first month the LORD named. Moses, Israel's leader, did it right on the day.

The answer is a cloud, friends! Moses, Israel's leader, finishes the work in verse 33, and then the cloud covers the Tent of Meeting. The verse says “…the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.” Verse 35 adds that Moses was unable to enter the Tent of Meeting because the cloud had settled on it. Bases, frames and crossbars all set up, and then this happens.

The answer is False. The text says, “Moses was unable to enter the Tent of Meeting because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.” Moses, Israel's leader, just finished the whole job and he can't go in. The cloud has settled on it.

The answer is that they set out on their journey. The text says, “Whenever the cloud was lifted from above the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out through all the stages of their journey.” The cloud lifts, and the people move. They know when to go by watching it.

The answer is fire. The text says, “…and fire was in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel through all their journeys.” A cloud by day, fire in the cloud by night. And everybody in Israel could see it.
